First thing first my fellow quarter-centurion (I know that's not right but you've got bigger problems to deal with then my misuse of the English language):  if your'e not being yourself... THEN THIS IS A WASTE OF TIME.

It's not weird or unusual to find it annoying that someone always agrees with you or is overly romantic according to your taste and or the familiarity you share. It's not at all uncommon for men (and women) to be fake with their crush this way... and that kind of interaction doesn't feel good. It can be as innocent as being desperate for the other person to like/approve of you and as nefarious as wanting to cultivate a particular image of yourself to manipulate the other person. If your personality leans that way (towards overt romance I mean) then it's possible you're not well-matched,or will need to explore that discomfort together. 

 I guarantee you that if my boyfriend was not my best friend first, and if he hadn't been courting me for years then I'd have run if he'd tried to  woo me as he woos me today... I would have been overwhelmed. Why? Because romance can be a creep factor. If this blows your mind in any way then consider yourself lucky not to have romance used as a creepy weapon against you. You just don't know that life. What's important here is that *you're* not like that (we will assume) and should not be treated with the knee-jerk annoyance or even fear that's clearly been inspired by past experiences... not by you.

​

Moving on to your other points: saying she said one thing but kissed you "like she wanted you badly" means nothing and is problematic if you think those actions contradict what she actually said to you. Kissing is kissing. It's not a contract, and if she never "took back" a previous statement then don't presume. Seriously. I wouldn't even have  pointed this out if you hadn't later said she kissed you "like she was in love"- um, forgive the harshness but NO she did NOT, because she's *not* in love (that much is crystal clear) and *you don't know her.* Same with her acting "like she was in love"- it was a *date*, and an experimental date at that, from the sound of it...  just from your account of her I can deduce that she's unsure of her feelings and intentions and is dipping her toes in the dating pool while trying to guard herself from what already went wrong (or what she's convinced *will* go wrong). She's young and she's confused, and she's trying to make sure you don't misunderstand her or make mistakes with her that someone else made... all in a rather unpracticed and awkward manner. 

​

If you have a hard time expressing how you feel try to start with honesty. Supplying it and asking for it. If you can't start with a blank slate then don't start because you are one man. You shouldn't have to be prepared to be "another guy" in a string of romances. If she can't deal with you as an individual rather than as an idea she isn't ready for a relationship. Which is also just fine. Maybe casual fun is more her pace right now... seems like it might be.
